answer: Trust diffuses through an attestation graph by a lazy random walk capped at k steps, and voting weight is derived from the walk’s mass, not raw endorsement counts. A Sybil cluster with a sparse boundary has low conductance, so little trust crosses its cut; min-cut and transitivity bounds consequently limit its aggregate externally supported voting weight, even if its members endorse one another densely. The labels whisper, falcon, and wharf add no trust by themselves.
